# Runbook: ${problem_category} incidents

**Who it's for:** first-line service desk (${first_line_group}) and the owning resolver group.
**Why it exists:** ${problem_category} is ${problem_share}% of tickets but ${problem_breach_share}% of SLA breaches. Only ${problem_first_line_share}% are fixed at first line, and ${problem_awaiting_user_rate}% stall waiting for user information. See `problem_review_rca.md`.
**Most common subcategory:** ${problem_top_subcategory} (${problem_top_subcategory_share}% of the category).

> The source data is anonymised, so the technical fix steps below are a template. Fill in the product-specific commands once the category's real service is confirmed. The process steps (intake, timings, escalation, comms) apply as written.

## SLA targets used by this runbook

These targets are the desk's own policy, not taken from the data (the data only says whether an SLA was met). The live desk in `power-automate/` uses the same ones.

| Priority | Resolve within | Warn the assignee at | Escalate to the lead at |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| P1 Critical | 4 h | 75% of time used (3 h) | breach |
| P2 High | 8 h | 75% (6 h) | breach |
| P3 Moderate | 72 h | 75% (54 h) | breach |
| P4 Low | 120 h | 75% (90 h) | breach |

## 1. Triage (first 10 minutes, on the first call)

Ask all of these before you save the ticket. Missing answers are the main reason these tickets stall in "Awaiting User Info".

1. What exactly were you trying to do, and what happened instead? Get the exact error text or a screenshot.
2. When did it last work? Has anything changed since then (new device, password change, update, move)?
3. Is it just you, or are colleagues affected too? *(If 5 or more users or a whole site are affected, raise impact to High.)*
4. Which device, asset tag and location?
5. Can you work at all? Is there a workaround? *(This sets urgency.)*
6. Is there a deadline or business event at risk in the next 24 hours?

Set **impact** (one user = Low, a team = Medium, a site or service = High) and **urgency** (has a workaround = Low, slowed down = Medium, fully blocked = High). Priority comes from impact × urgency, so don't override it by hand.

## 2. Checks before you fix anything

1. **Search open incidents** in ${problem_category} for the same symptom in the last 24 h. If you find 3 or more, link them and tell the lead that this is a possible major incident.
2. **Check problem records and known errors.** Only ${problem_problem_link_rate}% of these tickets are linked to a problem today, so link the ticket whenever one matches.
3. **Check the knowledge base** for ${problem_top_subcategory}. Attach the article you used, even if it didn't work, and say so in the work notes.
4. Confirm the user's account is active and not locked, and that the device is on the network and up to date.

## 3. First-line fix (aim: resolve within 30 minutes)

1. Follow the knowledge article for the subcategory. *(Add the steps here once confirmed.)*
2. Apply the standard reset: sign out and back in, clear the cached credentials or profile for the application, then restart the device.
3. If it's fixed, resolve the ticket with the fix written out, the KB article attached and the closure code set. Confirm with the user before closing.
4. If it's not fixed within 30 minutes of hands-on work, **escalate. Don't keep holding the ticket.**

## 4. When and to whom to escalate

| Condition | Escalate to | How |
|---|---|---|
| First-line fix failed, or it needs admin access first line doesn't have | **Owning resolver group** (proposed: ${fastest_l2_group}, the fastest second-line group for this category, with a median of ${fastest_l2_median_h} h) | Reassign once, with work notes covering what was tried, the triage answers and the error text |
| P1 or P2, or 5+ users affected | Desk lead **and** the owning group at the same time | Phone the lead and reassign. The lead decides whether to declare a major incident |
| 3+ similar tickets in 24 h | Problem manager | Open or link a problem record |
| 75% of SLA time used | Assignee gets an automatic warning | SLA Watch flow (`power-automate/`) |
| SLA breached | Desk lead | Automatic escalation email. The lead reassigns or swarms |

**Rule:** a ticket should be reassigned **once at most**. A reassigned ticket in this category has a median of ${problem_med_h_reassigned} h against ${problem_med_h_not_reassigned} h when it isn't reassigned. If the receiving group thinks it's the wrong group, they contact the desk lead rather than bouncing the ticket back.

## 5. Keeping the requester updated

| When | Message |
|---|---|
| Ticket logged | "Your request **[ID]** is logged as **[priority]**. We aim to resolve it by **[SLA due time]**. Reply to this email with any screenshots." *(sent automatically)* |
| Waiting on the user | Say exactly what you need and by when. If there's no answer, chase after 1 business day and again after 2, then resolve with a "reopen if still needed" note. |
| Escalated | "We've passed this to **[group]**, who specialise in this issue. Your reference stays the same." |
| Every 24 h while open (P3/P4), every 2 h (P1/P2) | A short progress note, even if there's no change. |
| Resolved | What was wrong, what was done, and how to reopen within 5 days *(sent automatically)*. |

## 6. Close-out checklist

- [ ] Fix and root cause written in the resolution notes
- [ ] Knowledge article attached, or a request raised to create one
- [ ] Problem record linked, if one applies
- [ ] Category and subcategory corrected if they were wrong at intake
- [ ] User confirmed the fix, or no reply after the chase cycle
